root_cause_label: Script Rounds Average To Two Decimal Places Writing 11.43 Instead Of Full-Precision 11.428571428571429, Then Agent Discovers Correct Value But Never Updates File Or Signals Completion
one_sentence_failure_summary: The Python script created at step 6 wrote the rounded value 11.43 to avg_temp.txt instead of the full-precision float 11.428571428571429, and after manually verifying the correct value at step 9 the agent neither corrected the file nor issued any completion signal.
t_err_evidence: Step 6 creates /app/calculate_avg_temp.py with a rounding operation that saves only two decimal places; the decisive mistake is baked into the script before execution.
t_commit_evidence: Step 7 executes the script which prints 'Average temperature difference: 11.43 F' and 'Saved to avg_temp.txt', writing the wrong rounded value to the output file and locking in the incorrect result.
t_surface_evidence: Step 8 reads /app/avg_temp.txt and the output shows '11.43', which is an observable wrong-output signal (expected full-precision 11.428571428571429).
trigger_explanation: The agent's plan was correct (parse heterogeneous date formats, compute per-day differences, average them), but code generation defaulted to rounding the result to two decimal places instead of preserving full Python float precision, a code-quality defect rather than a reasoning error.
